mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative correlation between GDPC1 decline and SPX returns breaks down for three consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods for two consecutive years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or the interaction effect is not significant in a multiple regression at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months indicates a compositional shift in the labor market (e.g., more people entering the labor force), which does not directly harm earnings and may be neutral for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which dampens consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered periods for three consecutive quarters.
